correctness.rationale: Independent rerun of inputs/artifacts/verify.py on audit hardware (Python 3.12.3, numpy 1.26.4, sympy 1.12) reproduces all claimed counts in 1.9s: 2^20+2^16+2^12=1118208 Frobenius tables, raw survivors 132+10+2=144, iso types 10+5+1=16, D<=12 raw 20+6+2=28 iso 3+3+1=7. Orbit recount with independent BFS confirms 35/30/25 total orbits, 15/14/13 fixed, 20/16/12 free. Independent pure-stdlib brute force for two-pair (4096 tables) gives 2 survivors and for one-pair (65536 tables) gives 10 survivors, matching verifier. All 16 canonical tables in tables.json pass independent pure-Python checks: 25/25 matrix identities Ni*Nj==sum_k Nijk*Nk, triple form sum_m Nij^m Nmk^l==sum_m Njk^m Nim^l, N0=I and Nij^0=delta_{j,i*}, lex-min minimality under 24/4/8 duality-preserving perms, SHA256 match, M=sum Ni strictly positive. Charpolys recomputed with sympy factor exactly as claimed: lam^4(lam-5), lam^3(lam-6)(lam-2), lam^3(lam^2-9lam+16), lam^2(lam-1)(lam^2-8lam+4) with Perron roots 5, 6, (9+sqrt17)/2~6.5615528, 4+2sqrt3~7.4641016. Exact quadratic-field eigenvectors verified: (1,1,1,1,1), (1,1,1,2,1), (1,1,1,(1+sqrt17)/2,1) using x^2=x+4, (1,1,sqrt3,2,sqrt3) variants, all satisfy Ni*d==di*d exactly (sympy simplify==0) giving D=5,8,(17+sqrt17)/2~10.56155,12. Bisection with exact Fraction evaluation gives Perron intervals width 5.96e-08 <1e-6. High-D exclusion recomputed in exact Fractions: all 9 logged rational vectors give L=sum li^2 with li=min_j (Ni*x)_j/x_j in {14,16.6044,24,26.1795,30.1376,31.0894,34.6427} all >12 (min margin 2), sound by Collatz-Wielandt for nonnegative Ni (Ni^k*x>=mu^k*x gives rho(Ni)>=mu). Commutativity Nijk==Njik holds for all 16 canonicals (hence all 144 raw by iso-invariance); self-dual=>commutative lemma verified via Nijk=N_{j*i*}^{k*}. Frobenius necessity lemma checked: tau(Xi*Xj)=Nij^0, tau((XiXj)Xk)=Nij^{k*}, tau(Xi(XjXk))=Njk^{i*} gives Nij^{k*}=Njk^{i*}, yielding orbit generators f1:(i,j,k)->(i*,k,j), f2:(k,j*,i), f3:(j*,i*,k*) as true symmetries; fixed-orbit consistency asserts pass; nonempty filter is sound for fusion rings since di*dj=sum_k Nijk*dk>0 requires >=1 k. No boundary error, no overflow (values <=5 in int16), no failed assert.

originality.rationale: Live retrieval (arXiv total 3, Crossref total 1810718) and inspection of four distinct sources shows no prior publication of the same bounded-stratum closure certificate. Vercleyen-Slingerland 2205.15637 generates all fusion rings to order 9 via single Wolfram pipeline and introduces songs generalizing TY/HI with data website, but provides no independent integer-auditable rank-5 D<=12 certificate with 25 residual tables, Sturm-isolated Perron polynomials and 2s rerun. Thesis 2405.20075 gives algorithms, Anyonica F/R-solving and appendices listing multiplicity-free rings to rank 9 / categories to rank 7 via same pipeline, not an independent audit. Vercleyen 2507.00652 explicitly questions whether Anyonica/anyonwiki census to rank 7 is a proper classification and resolves inequivalence only conditionally on correctness, directly evidencing the uncertified gap this work closes for one slice. Liu-Palcoux-Ren doi:10.1007/s11005-022-01542-1 classifies Grothendieck rings of multiplicity-one to rank six at journal level focusing on complex/categorifiable cases, not a from-scratch ring-level census including non-categorifiable rings with explicit Ni tables and Collatz-Wielandt exclusion. Underlying ring list may overlap prior tables (draft honestly states novelty is closure certificate not new bound/model), but bounded-stratum completeness plus rerunnable integer evidence for D<=12 with paired TY/pointed witnesses and noncommutative exclusion has no substantive prior equivalent.

value.rationale: Result is independently worth finding later, not a textbook restatement, parameter substitution, tiny gain or unexplained enumeration. It closes a citable gap flagged as conditional (Vercleyen 2025) for one FP-bounded stratum with reusable artifacts: 7 explicit lex-min Ni tables at D=5,8(x2 duality variants), (17+sqrt17)/2(x2),12(x2) with dimension polynomials and Perron intervals, 9 high-D types excluded by certified rational lower bounds L>12, and clean theorem that no noncommutative multiplicity-free rank-5 Frobenius-reciprocal ring exists at any D (anticipated collapse framed as exclusion). Identifications (Z5 pointed, TY(Z2xZ2)/TY(Z4) at D=8, near-integral sqrt17/sqrt3 families) give benchmark reference for tensor-category / anyon (Anyonica/anyonwiki) completeness discussions. Full rerun in ~2s (<600s) with stdlib+numpy+sympy, no Wolfram/Anyonica, SHA-logged tables and exact quadratic-field checks make it independently replayable and citable as benchmark increment, exceeding fallback threshold (closed D<=12, no frontier needed).

residual_risks: Frobenius necessity lemma proof is sketched in draft (tau argument); auditor verified derivation and fixed-orbit asserts, but formal completeness rests on standard fusion-ring identities rather than machine-checked proof object.

Literature comparison is qualitative without importing Vercleyen appendix / Liu-Palcoux-Ren tables; exact label-to-label matching of the 16 types to prior numbers is left to future work and does not affect census correctness.
High-D lower bounds are sound but not tight to true D; tightness is not needed for >12 decision (min margin 2) and no near-degenerate Perron case occurs.
Scope is explicitly multiplicity-free rank-5 Frobenius-reciprocal rings only; higher multiplicities, higher ranks, and pentagon/categorifiability are out of scope and not claimed.
Rerun verified on single audit host (1.9s); portability assumes numpy int16 exactness for values <=5 and sympy exact charpoly, both low-risk.
